basis: Migration Discovery, File Transfer and Local Storage: the shares the hosts offer and what they expose, the file transfer tools installed, removable-media controls, and the direction of file movement (migration-discovery-analysis skill; convert-subsection-prompt 5.6). Slots reuse the 3.7 storage frame's captures; 3.7 keeps the isolation and rating view.

slots.question: Which shares do the hosts offer beyond the default and administrative shares, and what could they expose or receive?
Which data flows cross a zone boundary (OT to IT, IT to OT, to the internet or cloud), which side opens each one, and is it a push from OT or a pull into OT?
Which data flows run inside OT (database, file share, replication, message), and what do they move?
Which tools for ad hoc file transfer are installed, and on which hosts?
Is removable media (USB storage) restricted by policy?
Does any transfer pass through a proxy, DMZ, broker or scanning point, or does it go direct?

story_groups.title: how files move and in which direction

scope_note: the shares the hosts offer and who may open them, the file transfer tools installed, removable-media controls, and the paths files take and in which direction (including whether they pass a proxy). Leave name resolution (for example DNS or hosts-file entries), time, patching and backup tooling to their own subsections; a database or backup connection belongs here only when it moves files or data between hosts. The framework places a table above the bullets that lists, host by host, every share with who may open it, the file transfer tools installed and any removable-storage setting. Do not repeat any of that per host. Write one short bullet (one or two sentences, at most 40 words) for each of these findings the table cannot show, and no other bullets: (1) the shares open to Everyone with full access, all in one bullet naming each share and its host; (2) the file share connections to peers, by address; (3) the SysVol shares hosts keep open, all in one bullet naming the domain controller; (4) whether a web proxy is used. Name each site in full (Mackay, Rockhampton) and name the server that holds a share, never 'other servers'.
